1. Core Clinical Tension: A 36-year-old female migrant worker presented with a 9-month history of high spiking fevers, massive splenomegaly (25 cm long axis), pancytopenia, marked hypergammaglobulinemia (serum IgG 53 g/L), and an apparent autoimmune serological profile including positive ANA (1:320), anti-dsDNA, positive direct Coombs test, and hypocomplementemia (depressed C3 and C4). Misdiagnosed with refractory systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), she failed intensive quintuple immunosuppressive therapy (prednisone, cyclosporine, hydroxychloroquine, tofacitinib, and telitacicept), because chronic reticuloendothelial infection triggers profound polyclonal B-cell stimulation that meticulously mimics systemic autoimmunity.
2. Admission Breakpoint: The breakpoint occurs prior to repeat bone marrow aspirate microscopy and send-out molecular testing ('Definitive diagnosis was made through direct visualization of intracellular Leishmania donovani parasites in smear of bone marrow aspirate...').
3. Differential Distinctions: Systemic lupus erythematosus (ruled out by treatment failure on aggressive immunosuppression, extreme splenomegaly out of proportion to lupus, and visualization of intracellular protozoans), lymphoproliferative malignancy (ruled out by hypercellular marrow with erythroid hyperplasia lacking malignant clones), and plasma cell dyscrasia (ruled out by normal immunofixation without monoclonal paraprotein).
case_prompt:
A 36-year-old female migrant worker originating from Shanxi Province and living in Guangdong Province presented for tertiary medical evaluation due to a 9-month history of recurrent high fevers, joint swelling, profound fatigue, and progressive unintentional weight loss. Her past medical history was notable only for untreated asthma of 4 years' duration. She reported no domestic animal contacts or sick contacts, and her family history was negative for autoimmune or immunodeficiency disorders.

Over the preceding months, she was evaluated at two different medical centers where laboratory investigations revealed pancytopenia (hemoglobin 91 g/L, white blood cell count 2.0 × 10⁹/L, platelet count 73 × 10⁹/L), elevated inflammatory markers (C-reactive protein 35 mg/L, erythrocyte sedimentation rate 59 mm/h, serum ferritin 256 ng/mL), marked hypergammaglobulinemia (serum IgG 53 g/L), and multiple positive autoantibodies including antinuclear antibodies (ANA, titer 1:320), anti-mitochondrial antibodies (AMA-M2), anti-double-stranded DNA (anti-dsDNA), and anti-PM-Scl antibodies. Direct Coombs test was positive, and serum complement levels (C3 and C4) were reduced. Hepatic and renal function panels and serum and urine immunofixation electrophoreses (IFE) were normal. Abdominal imaging revealed massive hepatosplenomegaly with a spleen measuring 25 cm in its longitudinal dimension. Two separate bone marrow examinations at outside facilities revealed hypercellular marrow with erythroid hyperplasia and reported no diagnostic clues or malignant infiltration.

Presumed to have systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), she was treated sequentially with high-dose systemic glucocorticoids, cyclosporine, hydroxychloroquine, tofacitinib, and telitacicept (a BLyS/APRIL inhibitor). Despite intensive immunosuppression, low-grade fevers and pancytopenia persisted. Ten days following self-discontinuation of tapered prednisone and cyclosporine, she suffered a relapse of high spiking fevers up to 40.0°C and was admitted for comprehensive evaluation.

On physical examination, the patient appeared chronical ill and emaciated. Temperature was 39.8°C. Abdominal examination revealed massive splenomegaly extending past the umbilicus along with hepatomegaly, without peritoneal signs. Repeat laboratory testing confirmed persistent pancytopenia, elevated ESR, CRP, serum ferritin, and markedly elevated polyclonal IgG. Non-contrast abdominal CT redemonstrated massive hepatosplenomegaly without discrete focal visceral masses.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Patient met classification criteria for SLE based on fever, inflammatory arthropathy, autoimmune hemolytic pancytopenia, positive ANA, positive anti-dsDNA, positive Coombs test, and hypocomplementemia; however, she showed zero clinical or hematologic response to aggressive quintuple immunosuppression, and massive splenomegaly (25 cm) with extreme polyclonal IgG (53 g/L) was driven by reticuloendothelial parasitic infection.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: A presumable diagnosis of SLE was made. She then received high-dose glucocorticoids, cyclosporine, hydroxychloroquine, tofacitinib, and telitacicept (a BLyS/APRIL inhibitor). But her fever persisted with low level grade and pancytopenia showed minimal improvement.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Prolonged high spiking fevers, profound weight loss, massive splenomegaly, pancytopenia, and hyperferritinemia raised strong suspicion for lymphoid malignancy or secondary HLH, but repeat marrow evaluations showed reactive erythroid hyperplasia without neoplastic cells or hemophagocytosis.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Bone marrow examination reportedly revealed hypercellular marrow with erythroid hyperplasia, with no evidence of malignancy or parasites.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered in the setting of severe hypergammaglobulinemia (serum IgG 53 g/L) and cytopenias, but excluded by normal serum and urine immunofixation electrophoresis confirming polyclonal rather than monoclonal gammopathy.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Liver, renal functions and Immunofixation Electrophoresis (IFE) of Blood and Urine were normal.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Microscopic review of bone marrow aspirate smears directly revealed intracellular Leishmania donovani amastigotes (Leishman-Donovan bodies), corroborated by reference CDC molecular PCR, confirming visceral leishmaniasis (kala-azar) that achieved rapid defervescence within 48 hours and regression of splenomegaly upon treatment with liposomal amphotericin B.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Definitive diagnosis was made through direct visualization of intracellular Leishmania donovani parasites in smear of bone marrow aspirate (Figures 2A,B), which was further confirmed by the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention (CCDC).

editor_comments: High-fidelity distillation of visceral leishmaniasis misdiagnosed and mistreated as systemic lupus erythematosus due to striking polyclonal autoantibody induction. Clean admission breakpoint with zero mention of Leishmania, amastigotes, or amphotericin B.
